title: Custom `secondaryBackgroundColor`/`backgroundColor` not applied to derived `codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When you set a custom `theme.secondaryBackgroundColor` and/or `theme.backgroundColor` (but don't set `theme.codeBackgroundColor` / `theme.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`), code blocks and dataframe headers still use the default derived colors from the base theme instead of recomputing them from the custom colors.

By default, both `codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` should be `bgMix` = a 50/50 mix of `backgroundColor` and `secondaryBackgroundColor`. That derivation happens correctly in `createEmotionColors`, but then gets overwritten with the base theme value.

### Reproducible Code Example

`.streamlit/config.toml`:

```toml
[theme]
backgroundColor = "#ffffff"
secondaryBackgroundColor = "#FAFAF9"
```

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.code("print('hello')")
st.dataframe({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set the theme config above
2. Run the app
3. Inspect the code block background color

### Expected Behavior

Code background should be the mix of `#ffffff` and `#FAFAF9`, i.e. roughly `#FDFDFC`.

### Current Behavior

Code background is `#F8F9FB`, which is the *default* `bgMix` (`mix(#ffffff, #f0f2f6, 0.5)`), ignoring the custom `secondaryBackgroundColor`.

Same issue for dataframe header background (`dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`).

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: develop
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

### Additional Information

Root cause in `frontend/lib/src/theme/utils.ts` (`createEmotionTheme`):

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor =
  codeBackgroundColor ?? colors.codeBackgroundColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor =
  dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor ?? colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor
```

`colors` here is the *base* theme's colors, so when the config option isn't set, we throw away the correctly derived value from `createEmotionColors(newGenericColors)` and replace it with the base default.

Contrast with the correct pattern used for `link` / `codeTextColor` a few lines below:

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.link =
  linkColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.blueTextColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.codeTextColor =
  codeTextColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.greenTextColor
```

These two (`codeBackgroundColor` and `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor`) seem to be the only instances of this bug — other derived colors from `bgMix` (e.g. `darkenedBgMix*`) are not overwritten and should pick up the custom colors correctly.

Fix should be something like:

```ts
conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor =
  codeBackgroundColor ?? conditionalOverrides.colors.codeBackgroundColor

conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor =
  dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor ??
  conditionalOverrides.colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor
```

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16398)

Confirmed bug in theme color derivation: when `theme.backgroundColor` / `theme.secondaryBackgroundColor` are customized but `codeBackgroundColor` / `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` are left unset, those surfaces keep the base-theme `bgMix` instead of the mix of the custom colors. Root cause is in `frontend/lib/src/theme/utils.ts` (`createEmotionTheme`): after `createEmotionColors(newGenericColors)` correctly derives `bgMix`-based values, the overrides fall back to the base theme’s `colors.codeBackgroundColor` / `colors.dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` instead of the newly derived `conditionalOverrides.colors.*` (unlike the correct pattern used for `link` / `codeTextColor`). Fix is a one-line fallback change for each property; existing unit tests only cover empty config or explicit overrides, so they miss this case.

### Related Issues

- [#11950](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11950) — Same `dataframeHeaderBackgroundColor` theme option; different failure mode (incorrect rendering when the value includes alpha).
- [#11933](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11933) — Same header background theme option; styling does not extend through the scrollbar region.
- [#11348](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11348) — Custom `backgroundColor` / `secondaryBackgroundColor` not applied consistently to derived UI surfaces (multiselect dropdown).

No exact duplicate found.
